hook.say: Troy, the Hittites and the world's oldest monuments are all in Turkey. Five questions on ancient Anatolia!

outro.say: How many did you get? Comment your score!

questions.q: The ruins of which legendary city lie in Çanakkale Province?
questions.say: The ruins of which legendary city lie in Cha-nak-ka-leh Province?
questions.fact: Heinrich Schliemann began excavating Troy in 1870.
questions.sayAnswer: Troy! Heinrich Schliemann began excavating it in 1870.

questions.q: Göbekli Tepe, with the world's oldest known megaliths, is near which city?
questions.say: Go-beck-lee Teh-peh, with the world's oldest known megaliths, is near which city?
questions.fact: Its great stone pillars were raised more than 11,000 years ago.
questions.sayAnswer: Shan-luh-oor-fa! Its great stone pillars were raised more than 11000 years ago.

questions.q: Hattusa was the capital of which Bronze Age empire?
questions.say: Hat-too-sha was the capital of which Bronze Age empire?
questions.fact: Hattusa's ruins lie near Boğazkale in Çorum Province.
questions.sayAnswer: The Hittite Empire! The ruins lie near Bo-az-kaleh, in Chorum Province.

questions.q: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus stood in which modern Turkish town?
questions.say: The Mausoleum at Halicarnassus stood in which modern Turkish town?
questions.fact: It was the tomb of Mausolus, whose name gave us the word mausoleum.
questions.sayAnswer: Bodrum! It was the tomb of Mausolus, whose name gave us the word mausoleum.

questions.q: Which Anatolian kingdom is credited with minting the first coins?
questions.say: Which Anatolian kingdom is credited with minting the first coins?
questions.fact: Lydia's capital was Sardis; its early coins were made of electrum.
questions.sayAnswer: Lydia! Its capital was Sardis, and its early coins were made of electrum, a mix of gold and silver.
